national_raw_news.content: India and Nepal have announced a series of initiatives covering connectivity, energy, trade, education, healthcare and institutional cooperation during Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s State Visit to India. The outcomes include a development assistance package worth 15,000 crore rupees, new cross-border infrastructure projects, expanded access to Indian ports for Nepal’s transit cargo and eight Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) across key sectors. Among the major announcements is the launch of the Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service connecting Ayodhya in India with Janakpur in Nepal. India and Nepal have adopted a Joint Vision Document, laying out a roadmap for a future-oriented partnership between the two countries. New Delhi also announced a development assistance package worth 24,000 crore Nepali rupees for the Himalayan nation. The two countries signed eight agreements to strengthen cooperation in various fields, including healthcare, traditional medicine, the establishment of a satellite communication network and capacity-building training programmes, among others. The agreements were signed following talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, in New Delhi yesterday. Both leaders held wide-ranging discussions on bilateral, regional and global issues. Later, in a joint press statement, Prime Minister Modi said India-Nepal relations are woven together by shared history, faith, culture and deep people-to-people ties. He also announced the Joint Vision Document adopted by the two nations.

national_raw_news.title: IFFI 2026: WAVES Film Bazaar to conclude at IFFI in Goa today
national_raw_news.content: The fifth day of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) promises a vibrant mix of cinema, learning and creative exchange. The day’s programme features a panel discussion titled ‘Her Lens, Her Legacy, Her Liberty: Women Shaping World Cinema’, followed by a masterclass by Romanian filmmaker Bogdan Mureșanu on the fine line between reality and fiction. The day will also mark the conclusion of the 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar, with a special focus on creating more opportunities for emerging writers and creators. An important outcome of the 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar was the signing of an MoU between the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and Sony Pictures Networks India. The agreement launched the WAVES Bazaar × SPNI Content Creator Submission Initiative, opening up opportunities for writers, creators and production houses to pitch original fiction and non-fiction concepts in five languages. Artists and creators submitted content in formats such as fiction series, premium TV+ content, reality shows, game and competition formats, talent-based programmes and other unscripted concepts. WAVES Bazaar connects creative talent with stakeholders across India’s media and entertainment ecosystem. Gaurav Banerjee, Managing Director and CEO of Sony Pictures Networks India, said the partnership with NFDC through WAVES Bazaar was a step towards creating more avenues for writers and creators. Initiated in 2007 as Film Bazaar with just 204 delegates, it has evolved into WAVES Film Bazaar and grown into one of South Asia’s leading platforms for film business and international collaboration. Another major highlight today at IFFI 2026 is the awards ceremony of the first edition of ‘Page Se Pitch Tak’. Conceived by Prasar Bharati Chairman Prasoon Joshi, the initiative was launched at the 57th edition of IFFI, giving emerging writers an opportunity to pitch original scripts in ten Indian languages across feature films, documentaries and short films. IFFI 2026 continues to witness cinematic buzz, with cinephiles thronging the festival venues to soak in the magic of cinema!

national_raw_news.title: Nation celebrates 557th Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji
national_raw_news.content: The 557th Parkash Purab of the founder of Sikhism, Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, is being celebrated today with religious fervour and enthusiasm across the country and abroad. Guru Sahib was born on this day in 1469 to Mehta Kalu Ji and Mata Tripta Ji at Rai Bhoi Ki Talwandi, now known as Nankana Sahib in Pakistan, on the full moon day of the month of Katak. Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji gave the message of ‘Ek Onkar’ (One God), opposed social evils such as casteism and emphasised the equality of all human beings. On this auspicious occasion, a large number of devotees have been paying obeisance at Gurdwaras across the country since morning. Gurdwara Ber Sahib at Sultanpur Lodhi in Punjab, where Guru Sahib meditated for 14 years, 9 months and 13 days, is reverberating with hymns as Kirtan Darbars and Gurbani Vichar are being held there and at other Gurdwaras, including Sri Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. The joy of connecting with God is evident on the faces of the devotees. Community kitchens are also being organised at various places. A delegation of Sikh pilgrims has also reached Gurdwara Sri Nankana Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Nanak Dev Ji in Pakistan, to pay obeisance. Deepmala and fireworks will be held at Sri Harmandir Sahib and other Gurdwaras this evening.
